title: A pull-down assay using DNA/RNA-conjugated beads with a customized competition strategy: An effective approach to identify DNA/RNA binding proteins
author: Sui, Chen, et al.

steps.title: Prepare nucleic‑acid‑conjugated beads
steps.instruction: Obtain Dynabeads® M‑280 Streptavidin (Invitrogen) that are pre‑conjugated with biotinylated DNA or RNA (e.g., full‑length pCR2.1, double‑stranded siRNA).

steps.title: Generate cytosolic fractions
steps.instruction: Lyse the appropriate cells (e.g., untreated HEK293 cells, IFN‑α‑treated HeLa cells) and collect the cytosolic extract using a standard protocol.

steps.title: Add nucleic‑acid competitor
steps.instruction: For competition assays, mix a 10‑fold excess of the chosen competitor nucleic acid with the cytosolic fraction before bead incubation. Competitors used in the examples include pCR2.1 DNA, non‑human control siRNA, plasmid DNA, Ctrl‑siRNA, mm‑siRNA (motif in the middle), or 3′m‑siRNA (motif at the 3′ terminus).

steps.title: Incubate extracts with beads
steps.instruction: Combine the cytosolic fraction (with or without competitor) with the DNA/RNA‑conjugated magnetic beads and incubate under the conditions described in the study (incubation time and temperature not specified).

steps.title: Separate bound proteins
steps.instruction: After incubation, collect the beads and resolve the bound proteins by SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: Visualize proteins on gel
steps.instruction: Stain the SDS‑PAGE gel with Coomassie blue or silver stain, or transfer the proteins to a membrane for western blotting using appropriate antibodies (e.g., anti‑RIG‑I).

steps.title: Interpret competition results
steps.instruction: Compare the band patterns between competitor‑free and competitor‑containing samples: disappearance of bands at ~80 kDa and 70 kDa indicates loss of Ku70; disappearance of a band at ~102 kDa indicates loss of RIG‑I; persistence of a band when plasmid DNA is used as competitor shows that the protein does not bind that competitor.
